2012_034_041712regmtg.paragraph: Packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of April 17, 2012, held at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, whose consent agenda covered the March 20, 2012 meeting and workshop minutes and the February and March 2012 Treasurer's Reports. Assistant Superintendent for Business Services Mark S. Rajter certified total disbursements in period of $5,140,090.13 for February and $5,071,363.25 for March. Reports on health insurance under 2011 PA 54 and PA 152, district goals and MEAP results accompanied readings of Board Policies B-1209, K-1301, B-1401 and new I-1701, plus a closed session on negotiations.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, 7:00 p.m., April 17, 2012, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., except July and August.

**Recognitions**
Student representatives Asja Kepes (International Academy East) and Marcarius Coakley (Niles Community High School); the all-volunteer Facilities Study Team of 18 community members, with liaisons Mike Zinn and Stu Redpath; six Outstanding Teacher nominees, of whom Mark Cavataio (physical education, Wass Elementary) and Susan Pickering (media specialist, Smith Middle) were sent to Oakland Schools, Pickering also being named the district's overall Teacher of the Year with a free one-year car lease donated through the Suburban Collection; and the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, president Mike Cianciolo, which made $500 grants in fall and spring rounds totaling 110 separate grants.

**Consent agenda and March 20 minutes**
Items A-C: March 20, 2012 board meeting minutes, March 20, 2012 workshop minutes, and the February and March 2012 Treasurer's Reports. At the March 20 meeting Vice President Edmunds presided (President Philippart absent); Resolution 12-026 approved consent items A-G by 6-0, Resolution 12-027 rescinded the $3,036.00 Bid 9723 award to National Educational Music Company for a Yamaha low E-flat bass clarinet, and Resolution 12-028 awarded the instrument to Midwest Musical Import for $5,520.00 as an expenditure of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. The workshop covered MEAP results, technology, email retention and board self-evaluation, adjourning at 9:47 p.m.

**General Fund budget position (Funds 101, 120, 122, 140)**
Against an approved revenue budget of $131,452,890 and expenditure budget of $130,078,102, February YTD actual revenue was $73,838,175 (43.83% uncollected) and actual expenditures $68,976,846 with $37,136,008 encumbered (18.42% available); March YTD actual revenue was $85,444,297 (35.00% uncollected) and expenditures $82,461,961 with $36,780,556 encumbered (8.33% available). Both reports show excess revenue over expenditures of 1,374,788, fund balance July 1, 2011 of 19,756,837 and projected June 30, 2012 fund balance of $21,131,625.

**Health insurance report (Jasen Witt)**
2011 PA 54 (signed June 8, 2011) and 2011 PA 152 (signed September 27, 2011) drive the changes; the PA 152 hard cap is $5,500 single, $11,000 employee-plus-spouse and $15,000 family, with an elective 80/20 option requiring a two-thirds board resolution and a 10% state-aid penalty for non-compliance.

**Curriculum reports**
Dr. Rich Machesky presented district goals in literacy, math, science and social studies keyed to 2012-2013 and 2013-2014 milestones; Anne Mull presented 3-9 MEAP results, including writing proficiency of 78 then 74 in grade 4 and 71 then 69 in grade 7.

**Policies and closed session**
First reading of revisions to B-1209 (Abstention from Voting) and K-1301 (Distribution of Materials to Students); second reading and consideration of B-1401 (Minutes) and new I-1701 (Opting Out of Video Presentations); closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c).

Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting held at 7:00 p.m. on April 17, 2012 in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices are at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, and meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except in July and August.

**Recognitions.** Student representatives were Asja Kepes of International Academy East and Marcarius Coakley, a senior at Niles Community High School. The Facilities Study Team, 18 volunteer community members who reviewed all district buildings, received small plaques; liaisons were Mike Zinn and Stu Redpath. Of six Outstanding Teacher nominees, a TEA selection committee sent Mark Cavataio, physical education teacher at Wass Elementary, and Susan Pickering, media specialist at Smith Middle School, to Oakland Schools; Pickering was also named the district's overall Teacher of the Year and awarded a free one-year lease of a car donated through the generosity of the Suburban Collection. Certificates and plants also went to Debbie Brorson (Schroeder), Pamela Mulligan (Hill), Gretchen Vogelei (Martell) and Glenn Rexer (Smith Middle). The Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, led by president Mike Cianciolo, awards $500 grants in every school and funded fall and spring rounds totaling 110 separate grants.

**Consent agenda and prior minutes.** Item 5 comprised the March 20, 2012 board meeting minutes, the March 20, 2012 workshop minutes, and the Treasurer's Report for February and March 2012. The March 20 meeting at the Troy Center for Transition was called to order at 6:00 p.m. by Vice President Edmunds with members Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present and President Philippart absent. Resolution 12-026 approved consent items A through G, including the January 2012 Treasurer's Report and bid awards for copy paper, air filters and utility vehicles, by 6 ayes and 0 nays. Resolution 12-027 rescinded the Bid 9723 award to National Educational Music Company for the Yamaha YUCL-621 low E-flat bass clarinet in the amount of $3,036.00; Resolution 12-028 awarded it to Midwest Musical Import for $5,520.00 as an expenditure of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. Judy Gail Armstrong-Hall spoke on money-saving initiatives and future science education needs; adjournment was at 6:10 p.m., minutes submitted by Secretary Todd Miletti. The workshop, on MEAP results, technology, email retention and the board self-evaluation, adjourned at 9:47 p.m.

**Item 6.A - District Health Insurance Update**, by Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent of Human Resources. 2011 Public Act 54, signed June 8, 2011, amends PERA at MCL 423.215b, barring employer cost increases after contract expiration, step increases, lane changes and retroactive pay increases, and requiring employees to absorb insurance cost increases by wage deduction. 2011 PA 152, the Publicly Funded Health Insurance Contribution Act, MCL 15.561 et seq., signed September 27, 2011, applies to coverage years beginning on or after January 1, 2012 and caps employer payments at $5,500 per employee with single coverage, $11,000 for employee plus spouse and $15,000 for family, adjusted annually by the Medical Care Component of the CPI; its elective 80/20 option requires a two-thirds board resolution, contracts in effect on or before September 15, 2011 are grandfathered but extensions are not, and non-compliance costs 10% of State Aid. BCBSM plans for non-rep, administrators and TESPA are CB 4 PPO ($500/$1,000 deductible, 80% coinsurance, $1,500/$3,000 out-of-pocket maximum), CB 3 PPO ($250/$500, 80%, $1,000/$2,000) and CB 2 PPO ($100/$200, 90%, $500/$1,000), all with $50 emergency room copay and $10/$40 prescription drug. Teachers and secretaries are on MESSA with $500/$1,000 deductible, 100% coinsurance, $20 office visit, $25 urgent care, $50 emergency room and Saver Rx; Pak A monthly rates for 7/1/11-6/30/12 include single rates of $657.17, $698.60 and $663.55 and family rates of $1,622.19, $1,663.62 and $1,613.50, with six-month trended rates for 7/1/12-12/31/12 reaching family $1,737.78 at 5% and single $756.44, two-person $1,583.13 and family $1,808.93 at 10% for teachers hired before 6/4/91. Trend citations: Segal 2012 medical/Rx PPO 9.5%, dental 3.8%, vision 3.8%; BCBS Michigan facility 10.19%, physician 11.56%, prescription drugs 12.98%, combined 11.28%; health care trend 9%-12% and prescription drugs 13%-14% with specialty drugs at +21%. HSA-eligible high deductible plans require minimum deductibles of $1,200 single and $2,400 family and cover preventive services at 100%. Next steps involve TESA secretaries and TEA teachers, both under contracts through June 30, 2013.

**Item 7.A - District Goals Overview**, by Dr. Rich Machesky, Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction. Goals include 100% of fourth grade teachers observing other classrooms four times by the end of 2012-2013 and 100% of fifth grade teachers by the end of 2013-2014, full K-12 balanced literacy materials by the end of 2012-2013, alignment of the secondary math sequence to the common core with materials selected for 2013-2014, data-interpretation training and claim-evidence-reasoning writing in grades 6-11, and expansion of MI CLASS/HI CLASS literacy training from 12 middle school social studies teachers to 24 teachers in grades 6-12, under a Vision 2013 framework using Atlas Rubicon, TEAM evaluation and NCA external review.

**Item 7.B - District MEAP Results**, by Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment, covering grades 3 through 9 in math, reading, science and social studies with old and new cut-score series from 2005-06 through 2011-12. MEAP writing proficiency was 78 in 2010-11 and 74 in 2011-12 for grade 4 and 71 then 69 for grade 7, with the note that a new writing test appeared in Fall 2010 and no new cut scores were established for writing. Comparison charts plot Troy against Oakland County districts and percent economically disadvantaged. Planned work includes K-5 word study professional development, a Carol Jago literacy presentation on June 18, preparation for Common Core assessments in 2015, and a Quality Assurance Review in Fall 2013.

**Item 10.A - First Reading.** Revisions to Board Policy B-1209, Abstention from Voting, adopted April 8, 1975 and revised June 7, 1977 and January 16, 1979, would permit abstention only for a direct or indirect financial conflict of interest, an appearance of conflict, or an explicit statutory or bylaw prohibition. Revisions to K-1301, Distribution of Materials to Students, adopted April 19, 1976 and revised January 16 1979 and April 21, 1998, require prior approval of the superintendent or designee for outside distribution. The board's attorney reviewed both for compliance with state law, the Open Meetings Act and the Revised School Code.

**Item 10.B - Second Reading and Consideration.** Revisions to Board Policy B-1401, Minutes, adopted April 8, 1975 and revised March 15, 1977, January 16, 1979, March 17, 1998 and June 19, 2007, require proposed minutes to be available for public inspection within eight business days after a meeting and approved minutes within five business days after approval, with records available under the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, Act No. 442, PA 1976. New Board Policy I-1701, Opting Out of Video Presentations, lets parents notify the building principal or classroom teacher to opt a child out of non-district-produced videos; first reading of both occurred at the February 7, 2012 board meeting.

**Item 11.A - Closed Session.** Consideration of negotiations, entered by resolution as permitted by the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8 (c), with a roll call listing Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff and Miletti.
